title: Mechanize the deprecated-term prohibition + scrub the slips (chassis/forcing-seam/substrate/platform)
description: Memory did not hold — used deprecated terms a day after grounding them (#819). Build a mechanized deprecated-term register check over the enduring corpus (like E0091), and scrub this session's slips. comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Reconciled with #821 (the atomic owned rename cycle). My ad-hoc two-file corpus scrub (chassis->crosslink in act-to-affordance-map + snapshot-schema) was REVERTED — that scrub is #821's owned+reviewed job, not a freelance on this branch. #832 is scoped to the ENFORCEMENT: arm mdatron E0093 (anti_patterns in .mdatron/vocabulary.yaml) so deprecated terms cannot re-enter governed prose. Dependency: arming chassis + substrate requires #821 to clear them from the corpus first (else verify reds on the corpus). 'forcing seam' is armable independently (0 corpus usages; my slip); 'platform' is NOT armable as a bare pattern (collides with 'cross-platform' + the platform-engineer domain) — needs a precise pattern or is out of scope. My session's own durable additions (REQ-13/AC-13/escape-row, the design docs) are terminology-clean; the slips were in chat, not artifacts.

comments.content: Merged to main (PR #13). E0093 'forcing seam' deprecated-term block is live — pre-commit + CI hard-fail on the term in governed prose. chassis + session-substrate arm as #821's rename clears them (linked). The lint half of the linter/tracker migration is now a live gate on main.
